name: Dardanelles
note: Site of the WWI Gallipoli campaign.
description: The Dardanelles — the Hellespont of the ancient world — is the outer gate of the Black Sea, a long, narrow channel between the Aegean and the Sea of Marmara with Europe's Gallipoli Peninsula on one side and Asian Anatolia on the other. Myth swam it with Leander and Lord Byron swam it after him; armies have contested it from Troy, which watched its entrance, to the Gallipoli campaign of 1915, fought over these narrows at terrible cost. With the Bosporus it forms the Turkish Straits, governed since 1936 by the Montreux Convention.
